content_voiceover: Two more Wilms tumor associations worth knowing for boards. First, WAGR syndrome, caused by a deletion at chromosome eleven p one three involving both the WT1 and PAX6 genes. The mnemonic spells it out, W for Wilms tumor, A for aniridia, absence of the iris, G for genitourinary malformations, which can include focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and renal failure, and R for mental retardation, or developmental delay. Second, stage five Wilms tumor, which is a distinct category referring to synchronous bilateral renal involvement at diagnosis, seen in about five percent of all Wilms tumor patients. Because both kidneys are involved from the start, these patients carry a substantially higher risk of end-stage renal disease, eleven to twenty percent compared to just zero point six percent in patients with unilateral disease.
keypoints: WAGR syndrome, Wilms tumor, Aniridia, Genitourinary malformations, mental Retardation
Caused by chromosome eleven p one three deletion involving WT1 and PAX6
Stage five Wilms tumor means synchronous bilateral renal involvement at diagnosis
Stage five carries much higher end-stage renal disease risk, eleven to twenty percent
keypoint_voiceover: Two things to lock in. WAGR is your mnemonic, Wilms tumor, Aniridia, Genitourinary malformations, and mental Retardation, from an eleven p thirteen deletion hitting WT1 and PAX6 together. And stage five Wilms tumor is not about size or spread, it specifically means both kidneys are involved at diagnosis, which is why these patients face a much steeper risk of ending up with end-stage renal disease.
